paper_metadata.title: QuantumLeap: Hybrid quantum neural network for financial predictions

summary: The paper presents QuantumLeap, a hybrid deep quantum neural network for stock-price prediction on 24 securities, using 20 strides, 20 epochs, and a sliding window of 4 trading days. It reports empirical improvements over a classical neural network and ARIMA, with example RMSV values such as 2.83 vs 6.05 vs 8.37 for AAPL, but no specific quantum hardware, qubit count, or formal speedup is provided.

experiments.description: Hybrid deep quantum neural network (QuantumLeap) for financial time-series prediction of stock high prices using a quantum encoder, deep quantum network, and classical measurement network; evaluated on 24 securities over regression and 20-day extrapolation/prediction regimes.

algorithm.variant: deep quantum neural network with classical measurement network (QuantumLeap)
algorithm.ansatz: layered unitary quantum perceptrons / deep quantum network

problem_formulation.encoding_details: financial time-series windows of size 4 are mapped to complex state vectors and density matrices using low/high prices; one quantum network per stride predicts a later density matrix, and a classical network measures the maximum price from the output density matrix
problem_formulation.objective_function: maximize fidelity between predicted and target density matrices during quantum-network training; classical network predicts the maximum price reached by the security

problem_instance.description: Stock-price prediction for 24 securities from 1 Jan 2019 to 11 Sep 2020, with 407 trading days for training and 20 trading days for testing/extrapolation

dataset_specification.preprocessing: sliding window of size 4 over low/high daily prices; windows converted to complex state vectors and density matrices; output target is the maximum price at a later stride
dataset_specification.train_test_split: first 407 trading days for training, last 20 trading days for testing/extrapolation

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: partition time series with sliding window; use low and high values; create unnormalised input/output state vectors; normalize according to paper's Eq. (18); evaluate density matrices; train one hybrid network per stride
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: regression and extrapolation over 20-day horizon; relative error reported per stock and day; comparison against classical neural network and ARIMA using RMSV and Mann-Whitney-Wilcoxon test

implementation_details.classical_solver: Adam-trained classical deep neural network baseline; ARIMA baseline
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: stock time series partitioned into windows; low/high values encoded into state vectors; normalization of state vectors
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: classical measurement network extracts maximum price from predicted density matrix

speedup_claims.conditions: The paper reports better empirical performance for QuantumLeap on RMSV and relative error, but does not claim a formal asymptotic speedup.
speedup_claims.caveats: No complexity-theoretic or wall-clock speedup is quantified; only empirical accuracy comparisons are provided.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: computationally tractable in terms of number of hidden layers; dimensions scale with number of layers

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: No hardware or qubit count is reported; the work is a hybrid model with no demonstrated quantum computational advantage.
